usual_baseline: Many transfusions fall outside threshold. Only 21.4% met NICE thresholds and targets [1254]; 73.5% were inappropriate [1294]; 40.2% of units followed NICE [2539]; 34% used a threshold below 70 g/L in critical care [2967]. Back-to-back units without reassessment were 20.5% [2539]. Out-of-hours units were appropriate in 70.6% [2638].
fix_that_works: Teaching and ward posters of thresholds: back-to-back units 20.5% to 4.51%, reactions 2 to none, saving about £5493 a year [2539]. Teaching and an induction booklet: TACO assessment 58.8% to 90.9% [1294].
fix_that_fails: After teaching, 45.5% of transfusions were still inappropriate [1294], and only 50.4% of units followed NICE [2539]. Both re-audits were small.
consultant_advice: Worth doing but the finding is well known. Measure single-unit prescribing and reassessment between units, and reasons for higher thresholds, such as a loosely defined 'coronary history' with no ACS [1254]. Pre-operative iron treatment was 7% and is a better target.
